title: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for South Sudan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Please accept sincere condolences for your loss. Institutional fragility and the absence of comprehensive public online civil-registry or statutory gazette portals in South Sudan limit remote verification of domestic .gov.ss websites (several judicial and ministry portals are offline or fail security certificate checks). Therefore, this guide cites live agency and diplomatic mission pages alongside verified international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, WIPO Lex, Refworld, and HCCH) and foreign consular reciprocity notices, and it is vital to confirm current local procedures directly with authorities in Juba or an accredited embassy.

steps.title: Obtain medical certification and a Ministry of Health death certificate
steps.html:
• Request the attending doctor to issue a formal medical report; under South Sudanese procedure, deaths must be certified by a senior medical officer at Juba Teaching Hospital (or the treating state facility) before official vital records are released [1].
  • Obtain the official English-language death certificate and burial permit indicating the cause of death from the Ministry of Health authorities, which usually takes several working days once medical or post-mortem reports are complete [1][2].
  • Coordinate related civil identity updates or cancellations with the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration (DNPI) under the Ministry of Interior, which administers civil status and nationality records under the Nationality Act 2011 and 2024 civil registration regulations [12][13][14].

steps.title: Navigate police reports, post-mortems, and burial or repatriation logistics
steps.html:
• For any sudden, home, accidental, or unexplained death, notify the police immediately; officers record witness statements, move the body to a hospital mortuary, and may require a post-mortem and toxicology report before releasing a final cause of death [1].
  • Note that mortuary refrigeration and specialist pathology expertise for international repatriation are extremely limited outside Juba; at Juba Teaching Hospital, private pathologists issue the autopsy report in triplicate alongside the embalming certificate and certificate of non-infectiousness needed for repatriation [1].
  • Notify the deceased person's own diplomatic mission promptly (for example, UK relatives contact the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office at +44 (0) 20 7008 5000) to assist with local liaison and shipment of personal effects or documents [1].

steps.title: Determine court vs customary probate and estate administration
steps.html:
• South Sudan applies a dual legal system under the Judiciary Act 2008 and the Local Government Act 2009 (indexed in FAOLEX statutory records [3]): statutory estate matters and grants of probate or letters of administration fall to the Judiciary of South Sudan (County Courts and State High Courts established under Part Seven of the Transitional Constitution 2011 and the Judiciary Act 2008) [4][7], while family property and land succession inside local communities are often addressed through Customary Law Courts and traditional chiefs [4].
  • Verify standing early, noting that South Sudanese authorities recognize a living spouse, child, parent, or close adult relative in order, and do not recognize same-sex spouses or partners [1].
  • Engage a South Sudanese advocate to petition the competent High Court or County Court for formal letters of administration or probate (formally referenced across statutory instruments such as the Companies Act 2012 for share and asset transfers) [6].

steps.title: Claim civil service survivor pensions and final employment entitlements
steps.html:
• If the deceased person served in government or the civil service, inquire with the Ministry of Finance and Planning regarding survivor pensions, death gratuities, and contribution records under the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 and the Pension Funds Act 2012 [8][9].
  • For private, NGO, or contractual employees, contact the employer to settle unpaid salary, accrued leave, and end-of-service or occupational death compensation governed by the Labour Act (No. 64), 2017 [5].

steps.title: Complete non-Apostille consular legalization before cross-border use
steps.html:
• Note that South Sudan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so apostilles cannot be used and every cross-border certificate or probate order requires full consular legalization [11].
  • Outbound South Sudanese death certificates or court orders must first be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Juba before submission to a foreign embassy [10].
  • Foreign-issued probate, power of attorney, or vital documents intended for use inside South Sudan must first be authenticated by the issuing state's Foreign Ministry (such as the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office or the U.S. Department of State) and then legalized by an accredited South Sudanese mission such as the Embassy of the Republic of South Sudan in London (immigration/civil authentication fee GBP 20, commercial GBP 50, payable in cash) [2][10].

closingQuestion: Would you like help checking the local steps in Juba or the consular legalization chain for the receiving country?
